hooks.text: The Moon is not frozen; it is actively spinning right now.
Why do we never see the far side of the Moon?
The Moon hides its far side despite spinning on its axis.

title: The Moon Is Not Frozen in Space
description: The Moon isn't stationary; Earth's gravity braked its rotation until its day matched its orbital period.

beats.text: The Moon is not frozen; it is actively spinning right now.
beats.visual: Lick Observatory photograph of the full Moon, 1968

beats.text: Because we always see the same face, many people assume it never rotates.
beats.visual: LRO mosaic of the lunar near side, 2011

beats.text: But to hide its far side, the Moon rotates once every twenty-seven point three days.
beats.visual: LRO animation of lunar libration showing rotation over an orbit, 2013

beats.text: Early in solar system history, it spun much faster before Earth's gravity grabbed hold.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of the early molten Earth and young Moon, 2015
queries: Young Earth and Moon early solar system

beats.text: Tidal friction created massive rock bulges, slowing its spin over millions of years.
beats.visual: Diagram showing gravitational tidal bulges and frictional torque on the Moon

beats.text: That orbital brake is so powerful it even lengthens Earth's day by two milliseconds per century.
beats.visual: Diagram of ocean tidal bulges and Earth's rotational braking

beats.text: Meanwhile, that transferred energy pushes the Moon roughly four centimeters further away each year.
beats.visual: Photograph of Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector on the Moon, 1969

beats.text: Every large moon in our solar system is locked in this same gravitational dance.
beats.visual: Montage of round moons in the solar system, 2020
queries: Moons of the solar system montage

beats.text: This gravitational deadlock permanently hides a world that never stops turning.
beats.visual: DSCOVR EPIC photograph of Earth and Moon in deep space, 2015

better_than_last: Applied rule 23 and reviewer notes by making beat 1 a direct, high-impact claim and ending beat 9 with a complete sentence that seamlessly loops back to beat 1.
